stemMd: Which statement distinguishes vaccination from antibiotic treatment of a susceptible bacterial infection?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Vaccines remove the need for immune cells.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Antibiotics create antigen-specific memory by definition.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Vaccination aims to establish specific immune protection; an antibiotic acts on susceptible bacteria.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Vaccines and antibiotics are the same type of molecule.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Both necessarily kill every virus directly.

explanationMd: A vaccine presents an antigenic stimulus to develop protection, whereas an antibiotic inhibits or kills susceptible bacteria. Do not confuse immune preparation with direct antimicrobial action.

distractorRationale.d: They differ in composition and mechanism.
distractorRationale.e: Antibiotics do not generally target viruses.
distractorRationale.b: Their defining action is antibacterial, not immune memory formation.
